title: Proof-Carrying Finding (PCF v0.1) certificate
description: The PCF v0.1 wire format a party re-verifies OFFLINE. Reflects the object produced by framework.v2.evidence.pcf.to_pcf (and, wrapped as {"pcf_certificates":[...]}, by `evidence pcf-export`). The PCF cert is a PURE PROJECTION of the signed EvidenceCertificate embedded under `_crucible.certificate`: every authenticated field here (claim, subject, evidence.oracle_context.digest, oracle, verdict, provenance, grounding, id) is a deterministic function of that certificate. The m-of-n Ed25519 signature covers the EMBEDDED certificate's canonical bytes (under the crucible-evidence-v1 domain), so any lying-wrapper mutation of a projected field is detected by re-deriving the view. PCF_VERSION="0.1"; the claim vocabulary is pinned by PCF_VOCABULARY="pcf-classes/1".

id.description: The embedded certificate's cert_digest (bare hex sha256 of its canonical bytes).

class.description: The oracle-provable bug class; drawn from the pinned vocabulary.

statement.description: The first bound report sentence, else a derived 'CLASS confirmed by ORACLE' statement.

evidence.description: The evidence digest-set (PCF §4.5). `oracle_context` is one item carrying the retained value so the oracle is re-runnable (PCF 'complete'); each additional key is one raw artifact, referenced by digest.

digest.description: digest_payload(value); MUST equal the embedded cert's oracle_context_digest.

value.description: The retained oracle_context the oracle re-runs over.

additionalProperties.description: One raw artifact (key = its relative path).

version.description: The content-derived oracle id@version at mint time. REQUIRED for a FACT; a verifier rejects a version mismatch against the current oracle body (stale proof).

binding.description: The canonical verify binding, e.g. crucible/verify:<oracle_kind>.

fired.description: A PCF certificate exists only for a CONFIRMED finding.

domain.description: The domain-separation label; the signed bytes are b"crucible-evidence-v1\u0000" + canonical_json(embedded certificate).

sig.description: base64 of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature (note: the PCF wire member is `sig`, not `signature_b64`).

_crucible.description: The AUTHORITATIVE signed object the signature actually covers. A verifier reconstructs it, re-derives the signed bytes AND the projected view, and rejects any drift.
